title: Marie Curie's birth chart
metaDescription: Marie Curie's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.6° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Scorpio — the Sun, Venus, Mars and Saturn. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 14.6° Scorpio — the second decan, 10°–20°, which the tradition sub-rules by Jupiter. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Scorpio and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 6.6° Sagittarius, Venus at 25.6° Scorpio, Mars at 29.6° Scorpio. Mercury in a fire sign reads as a mind that decides at speaking speed; Venus in a water sign reads as taste tuned to mood and undertow; Mars in a water sign reads as drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Uranus and Neptune hold the closest angle here — a square, 0.1° wide. The old texts treat a square as the aspect you feel earliest and thank latest: obstruction first, competence afterwards. Behind it, Venus conjunction Saturn at 0.3°, and the Sun opposition Pluto at 0.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Sagittarius at 6.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Scorpio at 25.6° is in detriment; Mars in Scorpio at 29.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives water 6, fire 2, air 1, earth 1, and fixed 6, mutable 2, cardinal 2 across the modes. Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Pisces for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.7° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 16.5°.
